region_scene_page.compact: A 1960s ornate-pop road where chamber instruments, studio craft, close harmony, and emotional precision make pop feel miniature and grand at once.
region_scene_page.standard: Baroque pop does not mean classical music pasted onto rock. It means pop writers and producers using strings, harpsichord colors, unusual chord movement, and careful arrangements to give short songs a chamber-world glow. The Beach Boys, Left Banke, Zombies, Love, Procol Harum, and early Bee Gees each approach that glow differently. The lane is polished but fragile: orchestration, harmony, and bittersweet melody matter more than volume or jam energy.
